titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 4 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 4 of 4: the last titles of Ra, Ani's prayer to be glorified and to sail in the Field of Reeds, and promises of his voyage with the sun (Plate 21)
about: The fourth and last part of Spell 15 ends Ani's hymn to Ra on Plate 21. The list of the god's titles closes, and Ani prays that he be glorified in the necropolis, placed among the revered ones, joined with the bas in the Sacred Land and allowed to sail in the Field of Reeds. A last section, opened by a word written in red, promises him that he will cross the sky among the stars, see Ra in his shrine, the inet-fish and the abdju-fish, and Horus, and Thoth and Maat at his sides, while the enemy falls and all the gods rejoice. Budge's type is uncertain in many signs here, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: great · (of)-dread · power · (of)-the-powers · far(?) · seat · his · from · wrongdoers
sentences.i: Great of dread, power of the powers, whose seat is far(?) from the wrongdoers;
sentences.n: ꜥꜣ nrw 'great of dread' is the column ꜥꜣ with U15 (read ꜥ, as throughout these plates), the vulture ꜣ and the roll, then nrw 'dread' spelled out sign by sign (n-r-w-i-w; the i and the second w are not read): water n, r, the chick w, a reed and the coil w (a fuller spelling), with U15 and plural strokes as classifiers, where the word usually has the vulture (G14) that classifies it (Spell 17 on this papyrus also writes nrw without the vulture); Budge's numeral 35 stands inside it. 'Great of X' is an adjective with the thing it is great in. sḫm sḫmw 'power of the powers' is the sceptre sḫm with m and U15, then the sceptre again with a stroke and the seated god for the divine 'Powers': a noun followed by its own plural, 'the mightiest of the mighty'. ḥrw st·f r isftyw is taken as ḥri 'be far (from: r)', 'far is his seat from the wrongdoers', taken as a participle with the noun after it, 'far of seat', the same pattern as ꜥꜣ nrw: the face ḥr with r, w and U15, then st 'seat' (the seat Q1, t and a house sign) with ·f; Budge reads ḥeru, 'fortifying', and the reading is doubtful. isftyw 'wrongdoers' is i, the tall sign is (coded Y1a, approximate, as in isft), s, f, t and the vulture standing for the plural ending, as in ḫftyw, with a kneeling man struck on the head (A14, approximate) as classifier. The list of the sun-god's titles from the previous part goes on.

sentences.l: great · (of)-appearings · in · Sektet-bark · great · he · long(?) · in · Adjet-bark
sentences.i: great of appearings in the Sektet-bark, great is he and long(?) in the Adjet-bark.
sentences.n: ꜥꜣ ḫꜥw has the same pattern: ḫꜥw 'appearings' is the sun rising over a hill (N28) with ꜥ, w, the roll and a stroke, the god's shining forth. sktt, the evening bark (s, k, t twice and a boat on a stand, P3, approximate), and ꜥḏt, the morning bark (the netting needle ꜥḏ, V26, approximate, with t twice, the hand d and the boat; the short name the first part of the spell also has for the Mandjet-bark), are the barks of the sun's two journeys. wr·f is the swallow wr with r and ·f: 'great is he', the sḏm·f of the adjective-verb wr 'be great' with ·f as its subject (an adjectival sentence would have the dependent pronoun, wr sw). ꜣw after it is the spine with a cord at each end (F40) with w, the roll and a stroke, 'long, extended'; how it is joined to wr·f is not clear (Budge: āu, 'exceedingly'), and the rendering is doubtful. Budge's numeral 36 stands inside ꜣw.

sentences.l: glorify · you · Osiris · Ani · in · vindication · in · necropolis
sentences.i: May you glorify the Osiris Ani in vindication in the necropolis.
sentences.n: From here the hymn turns from praise to prayer. sꜣḫ·k 'may you glorify' is the bolt s, the ibis ꜣḫ (G25, approximate; no crest is visible in the print) with its complement ḫ (Aa1), the chick w (written as in ꜣḫw 'spirits', and not read in the verb), the roll and ·k: the causative of ꜣḫ, 'make (someone) an effective spirit', in the sḏm·f of wish. Wsir ꜣny 'the Osiris Ani', here with the kneeling man (A1) as Ani's classifier. m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: the bar m (Aa15) and the plinth and oar, written as usual without the sickle (the plinth is itself mꜣꜥ), used as a noun, 'vindication'. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr joined to the block ẖr (T28) with a loop r (approximate), t and the hill-land sign.

sentences.l: grant · you · be · he · at · West · free · of · evil
sentences.i: Grant that he may be in the West, free of evil.
sentences.n: di·k 'may you grant' (the arm giving a loaf, D37, and ·k) is followed by a second sḏm·f, wnn·f 'that he be' (the hare wn with n, n and ·f): rdi with a sḏm·f, 'cause that'. r imntt 'in the West' is the West sign (R14) with t twice and the hill-land; r is here 'at, in'. šw m ḏwt 'empty of evil': šw is the feather šw with w and the sparrow of lack, ḏwt 'evil' the mountain ḏw (N26, approximate), t, w, the sparrow and plural strokes. Budge's numeral 37 stands before šw.

sentences.l: see · behind · you · wrong
sentences.i: See, wrong is behind you(?).
sentences.n: mk 'see, behold' is the owl m with the arm (G17 and D36 printed as one ligature, approximate; m is often written mꜥ on this papyrus, and the arm is not read) and k. ḥꜣ·k 'behind you' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ and the back of the head (D1, approximate): the preposition ḥꜣ with ·k. isft 'wrong' is spelled as in isftyw above, with the sparrow and plural strokes. There is no verb: as it stands this is an adverbial sentence with the predicate put first, 'behind you is wrong' (after mk the subject usually comes first, mk isft ḥꜣ·k, so the order is unusual), that is, wrong is put out of the god's sight. Budge supplies a verb and a 'his' ('put behind thee [his] faults'; the [his] is in his English only). The sense is doubtful.

sentences.l: place · you · me · among · revered-ones · with · spirits
sentences.i: May you place me among the revered ones, with the spirits.
sentences.n: Budge's ṭā-kuà is one group; it is split here into di·k 'may you place' and wi 'me': the kneeling man (A1) alone writes the dependent pronoun wi, the object of rdi, as in mk-wi elsewhere on the papyrus. rdi m is 'put among'. The signs can also be read as one word, Budge's group: di·kwi, the stative of rdi with the 1st-person ending ·kwi written k and the seated man (as in nn·kwi elsewhere on the papyrus), 'I am placed among the revered ones'; both readings fit the signs, and the split is doubtful. imꜣḫyw 'the revered ones' is the spine with one hanging cord (F39), the imꜣḫ sign, with ḫ and two reeds y: the plural of imꜣḫy 'one honoured', the blessed dead who are provided for (Budge: àmχi); his numeral 38 stands inside it. ḫr 'with, near' is the placenta ḫ and r, the preposition used of persons. ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is the ibis ꜣḫ (G25, approximate) with ḫ, a kneeling figure holding a flail (A52, approximate) and a stroke. Ani speaks of himself here as 'me', and in the next clause again as 'he'.

sentences.l: be-joined · he · (with)-bas · in · Sacred-Land
sentences.i: May he be joined with the bas in the Sacred Land;
sentences.n: ḫnm·f 'may he be joined (with)' is the jug ḫnm (W9) with m, the roll and ·f, a sḏm·f of wish; ḫnm takes the ones joined as its object. bꜣw 'the bas' is the incense bowl (R7), the ba's classifier on these plates, with the ram bꜣ (E10, approximate) and two strokes, as in the second part of the spell. tꜣ-ḏsr 'the Sacred Land' is the strip of land tꜣ (N16, approximate), then a low sign coded U15 (approximate) that stands where the arm with the wand of ḏsr (D45) is expected, t twice and the hill-land. Budge reads Ta-sertet, so he took the low sign for ḏsr; the reading rests on his. The Sacred Land is the cemetery, the realm of Osiris.

sentences.l: sail · he · in · Field-of-Reeds · because · protection(?) · decreed · with · gladness-of-heart
sentences.i: may he sail in the Field of Reeds, because protection(?) has been decreed with gladness of heart.
sentences.n: sqdd·f 'may he sail' is the bolt s, the tall sign qd (Aa28, approximate), the hand d twice (Budge: seqṭeṭ), a small pot (W24, approximate; not read) and the boat on a stand as classifiers, and ·f: sqdi 'travel by boat', a sḏm·f taken as a wish like ḫnm·f before it. The hand is written twice, as in sqdt for the Sektet-bark in the previous part; it may be only a spelling, or the doubled form (sqdd·f) of this 3ae-inf verb, which is not usually the form of a wish, and the reading of the form is doubtful. sḫt-iꜣrw 'the Field of Reeds' is the field with t and the wedge (N21, approximate), then i, ꜣ, r, w with the reed plant, strokes and the town sign; Budge's numeral 39 stands inside it. Budge prints ḥer enti sa as three groups under one English word, 'through'. ḥr and nty are joined here into ḥr-ntt 'because' (the face with its stroke, n, t and the two strokes for the ending, as elsewhere on this papyrus), and sꜣ is read as a noun of its own: a box-like sign with a loop (coded Aa17, approximate; the protection sign V16/V17 is possible) with a stroke, taken as sꜣ 'protection'; this rests on an uncertain sign. wḏ is the staff wḏ (V24, approximate) with w and the roll, 'is decreed', the stative after its subject sꜣ, the usual pattern after ḥr-ntt (noun + stative). ꜣwt-ib 'gladness of heart' is the spine ꜣw (F40) with t and the heart: literally 'length of heart'. The clause after ḥr-ntt is doubtful as a whole.

sentences.l: says · Osiris · scribe · Ani · true-of-voice
sentences.i: So says the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice.
sentences.n: in, the reed and water, is taken here as 'says': in with a noun after the words quoted names the speaker, 'says N', and closes Ani's prayer. In Spells 18 and 146 in N stands before the words it introduces; here the words that follow speak to Ani as 'you', so it is taken as closing what comes before. Budge renders it 'O', a call that would open the address that follows; the call is usually i (as at the start of the previous part), so that reading is less likely, but it is possible, and this is doubtful. Budge's 'joy of heart' runs on under in; it belongs to ꜣwt-ib alone. Wsir is written short, the seat (Q2, approximate) over the eye with no god classifier; sš 'the scribe' is the palette alone (Y3, approximate); mꜣꜥ-ḫrw without the sickle, as before.

sentences.l: come-forth · you · to · sky
sentences.i: You shall come forth to the sky;
sentences.n: The papyrus writes pr·k in red: Budge marks it with a rule over the word, beginning at his numeral 40 (the readers differ on whether it reaches the walking legs and the basket ·k). A new section begins, a string of promises to Ani in the 2nd person. pr·k is the house pr with r, two reeds (a fuller spelling of pri, as Budge's peri shows; not read) and the walking legs, with ·k: the sḏm·f with a future sense, 'you shall come forth'. pt 'sky' is p, t and the sky sign.

sentences.l: cross · you · firmament · keep-company · you · among · stars
sentences.i: you shall cross the firmament and keep company among the stars.
sentences.n: ḏꜣ·k 'you shall cross' is the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) with ꜣ, two reeds and a boat on a stand (P3, approximate), with ·k: ḏꜣi 'cross (water)', used of the passage over the sky as over a river. biꜣ 'the firmament' is the foot b and the reed i with t (not read in biꜣ), a cup (W10, approximate) and a flat bar with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) over plural strokes as classifiers; the ꜣ is not written and no sky sign is printed (Budge: bàt, 'the sky'). biꜣ is the metal of heaven, and the sky as a vault of it. snsn·k is two arrowheads sn (T22, approximate) with the bar (Aa13, approximate) and ·k: the reduplicated verb, here 'keep company with' (Budge: sensen-k, 'thou shalt be associated'). m-m 'among' is the owl and then the owl with the arm, as in mk; sbꜣw 'the stars' is the star with a stroke and the seated god.

morph.gloss: the firmament, the sky as a vault of metal (here; the ꜣ not written; Budge: bàt, 'the sky')
to keep company with, be joined with (here, with m-m 'among'; Budge: sensen, 'be associated')
star (noun m.; plural sbꜣw; written with the star; Budge: sebu)

sentences.l: is-made · for · you · praises · in · bark
sentences.i: Praises are made for you in the bark;
sentences.n: Budge prints àritu-nek as one group, with his numeral 41 inside it; it is split here into ir·tw and n·k. ir·tw 'one makes, there is made' is the eye ir with r and the passive ending ·tw (t over the coil w): the sḏm·tw·f, with ḥknw 'praises' as its subject. n·k 'for you' is water n and ·k. ḥknw is the wick ḥ, k, n, the pot nw (W24, approximate; no oil jar is printed) with w, and a man with hand to mouth (A2), the classifier of speech, with a stroke: 'praise, hymn'. wiꜣ 'the bark' is w, i, ꜣ and the boat on a stand (P3, approximate).

sentences.l: is-called · you · in · Adjet-bark
sentences.i: you are called in the Adjet-bark.
sentences.n: nis·tw·k 'one calls you, you are called' is n, i, s with the man with hand to mouth as classifier, then the passive ·tw (t, w) and ·k: nis 'call, summon' (Budge: 'thou shalt be hymned'). ꜥḏt, the morning bark, is written here without the hand d, with a stroke after the boat (P3, approximate).

sentences.l: see · you · Ra · in · interior · of · shrine · his
sentences.i: You shall see Ra within his shrine;
sentences.n: dgꜣ·k 'you shall see' is the hand d over a jar stand g (W11, approximate), ꜣ, two reeds and the eye as classifier, with ·k: dgi 'look, behold'; Budge's numeral 42 stands before it. rꜥ is r, ꜥ (U15) and the god with the sun-disk. m ẖnw n kꜣri·f 'in the interior of his shrine': ẖnw is the animal's belly ẖ (F32, approximate) with n, the pot nw (W24, approximate) and a house sign, here a noun with n 'of' after it (Budge's 'within' stands under m and ẖnw together); kꜣri 'shrine' is the raised arms kꜣ, r, i and a shrine (O18, approximate), with ·f.

sentences.l: make-content · you · Disk · his · day · every
sentences.i: you shall make his Disk content every day.
sentences.n: sḥtp·k is s with the offering table ḥtp, t and p, and ·k: sḥtp 'make content, satisfy', the causative of ḥtp (Budge: 'thou shalt set with'). iṯn·f 'his Disk' is i, the tethering rope ṯ (V13), n and the sun, with ·f: the old spelling with ṯ, as in the previous part. hrw nb 'every day' is the sun with a stroke and the basket.

sentences.l: have-seen · you · inet-fish · in · coming-into-being · its · upon · water(?) · of · turquoise
sentences.i: You have seen the inet-fish in its coming into being upon the water(?) of turquoise;
sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·n·k 'you have seen' is the eye with the sickle mꜣ printed above it, the vulture twice, n and ·k: the sḏm·n·f, written so three times in this passage (Budge: maa-nek, 'thou shalt see'); the past tense stands among promises in the future, and it is kept as written; Budge's numeral 43 stands inside it. int 'the inet-fish' is i, the fish in, n, t and a second fish as classifier (both K1, approximate). ḫpr·s 'its coming into being' is the scarab ḫpr with r, a reed, a standing mummy-shaped figure (A53, approximate), the roll and a stroke as classifiers, and ·s (the bolt): the infinitive with a suffix for its subject. bꜥbꜥt is the foot b with ꜥ (U15), twice, and t over three water lines: a word for water (Budge: bābāt, 'the water'), not met in the earlier parts; its sense is doubtful. nt 'of' is n and t; mfkꜣt 'turquoise' is the owl with the arm (as in mk), f, k, t and a small round stone classifier with plural strokes; the ꜣ is not written. The inet-fish and the abdju-fish swim before the sun's bark.

sentences.l: have-seen · you · abdju-fish · (at)-time · its
sentences.i: you have seen the abdju-fish at its time.
sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·n·k as before. ꜣbḏw 'the abdju-fish' is the emblem of Abydos (R17, approximate) with b and the hand d, and a fish (K1, approximate) as classifier in place of the town sign: the same word as the name of Abydos. sp·f 'its time' is s, p and the threshing floor sp with ·f; no preposition is written before it (Budge: '[in] his season', with the [in] in his English only), and the noun is taken as an adverb, '(at) its time'.

sentences.l: may-come-about · evil · fall · … · as · has-foretold · he
sentences.i: May it come about that evil falls … as he has foretold(?).
sentences.n: ḫpr is the scarab with r: 'may it come about', a wish, with what follows as its content. ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw (N26, approximate) with t and w, followed by one sign that Budge prints as a row of small hanging looped strands, for which there is no good code (D3, approximate, as in ḫfty below); it stands where the sparrow of bad things would be (Budge: ṭutu, 'the Evil One'). ḫr 'fall' is ḫ, r and a falling man (A15); ḏwt ḫr, noun then verb, is taken as the content of the wish, 'that evil falls'; the form of ḫr is not clear: a stative after the feminine ḏwt would usually show its ending t, which is not written here. Before ḫr the sign line has an empty space, and Budge's transliteration has dots ('.....') there; he prints no signs and no brackets, so nothing is read or restored, but something may be missing. ḫft 'as, according as' is ḫ, f, t; sr·n·f 'he has foretold' is s, r and the giraffe sr (E27) with n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f of sr 'foretell, make known'. Budge reads 'when he setteth in order'; who 'he' is is not said, and the rendering is doubtful.

sentences.l: cut-off · for · me · pierced(?) · vertebrae · of · him
sentences.i: It is cut off for me(?), and his vertebrae are pierced(?).
sentences.n: Budge's ḥeseq-nà and θesu-nef are each split here: ḥsq n·i and ṯsw n·f. ḥsq 'cut off' is ḥ, s, the triangle q over a knife (T30, approximate), with U15 after it as in other spellings of the word, taken as a passive with no subject written, 'it is cut off'; n·i is water n and the kneeling man ·i, 'for me'. As it stands ḥsq n·i could also be a sḏm·n·f, 'I have cut off'; Budge reads 'destruction for me'. dmw is the hand d over the bar m, w and two knives: dm 'be sharp, pierce' (Budge: ṭemu, 'let be cut asunder'), taken as a passive sḏm·f, with the w the passive sometimes shows; his numeral 45 stands inside it. ṯsw 'vertebrae' is the knot ṯs with s, w and a backbone with spines (F37, approximate) over plural strokes, the plural of ṯst 'vertebra' with the t of the feminine not written; n·f 'of him' follows where ·f alone would be usual. The enemy of Ra is meant, as in the first part of the spell, where the knife has cut through the backbone of the enemy. The whole sentence is doubtful.

sentences.l: is · Ra · in · breeze · good
sentences.i: Ra is in a fair breeze;
sentences.n: wnn is the hare wn with n and n, the sḏm·f of wnn 'be' with rꜥ as subject, opening the clause; this form often looks to the future ('Ra will be'), as the promises around it do, and the present is a choice. mꜣꜥw is the sickle mꜣ (U1, approximate) over U15 (ꜥ), w and a sail (P5, approximate) as classifier of wind: read mꜣꜥw 'breeze, the fair wind for sailing' (Budge: maāu, 'winds'). nfr 'good' is the heart and windpipe nfr with f and r.

sentences.l: has-hauled(?) · Sektet-bark · reaches · him
sentences.i: the Sektet-bark has hauled(?) and reaches him;
sentences.n: sk is s, then a twisted cord crossed by a bowed bar with knotted ends (coded V28 as elsewhere in these plates, but with the bar of the swab sk, V29), k and U15; then water n with a stroke. Budge prints sek and en as two groups; they are joined here into sk·n, the sḏm·n·f of sk with sktt 'the Sektet-bark' as its noun subject, as in the first part of the spell (sktt sk·n·s pḥ sw), where the same words stand: 'the Sektet-bark has hauled'. The sense 'haul, tow' of sk is taken from Budge ('draweth onward') and is not certain; sk n sktt, 'one hauls for the Sektet-bark', with n as a preposition, is also possible. pḥ sw: pḥ 'reach' is the hindquarters pḥ (F22, approximate) with the walking legs; sw (the sedge sw with w) is the dependent pronoun 'him', the object, with the bark, unwritten, still the subject, as in the first part of the spell. sw is masculine and cannot be the bark (sktt is feminine); who 'he' is is not said, perhaps the god.

sentences.l: crew(?) · (of)-Ra · in · rejoicing
sentences.i: the crew(?) of Ra are in rejoicing.
sentences.n: qdt rꜥ m ḥꜥꜥwy is a sentence with no verb, a noun subject and m with a noun, like nṯrw nbw m ḥꜥꜥw 'all the gods are in rejoicing' below. qdt is the tall sign qd (Aa28, approximate), t, and a seated figure with a long wig (A40, approximate) between strokes: Budge reads qet, 'the sailors of Ra', and it is taken so here, 'the crew' of Ra in a direct genitive with rꜥ; the word is doubtful (the usual word for the crew of a boat is sqdw, from sqdi 'sail', with an s that is not written here). m ḥꜥꜥwy 'in rejoicing' is ḥ, ꜥ twice, y, w and a man with raised arms (A28, approximate), spelled as in the second part of the spell. Budge also reads two clauses here ('and arriveth it, the sailors of Rā are in rejoicing').

sentences.l: Nebet-ankh · heart · her · glad · felled · enemy · of · lord · her
sentences.i: Nebet-ankh, her heart is glad: the enemy of her lord is felled.
sentences.n: nbt-ꜥnḫ 'Lady of Life' is the basket nb with t, the ankh and a rearing cobra (I12, approximate) as classifier of a goddess; Budge leaves the name as Nebt-ānkh, and the text does not say which goddess is meant. ib·s nḏm 'her heart is glad' puts the noun first: ib 'heart' (the heart and a stroke) with ·s (the bolt), then nḏm, printed with the twisted wick (V28) where the sweet pod (M29) is expected, as in the first part of the spell, with m and the roll. Budge's English adds '[for]' in brackets; nothing stands for it in the signs. sḫr is s, ḫ, r with the falling man (A15) and U15: the causative of ḫr 'fall', taken as a passive sḏm·f, 'is felled' (Budge: 'fallen hath'), with its subject ḫfty 'the enemy' after it: ḫ, f, t and the row of hanging strands (D3, approximate) as in ḏwt above. n nb·s 'of her lord' is the genitive n and the basket nb with a seated figure (A40, approximate) and ·s (the folded cloth).

sentences.l: have-seen · you · Horus · at · the-neferu(?) · Thoth · Maat · at · two-arms · his
sentences.i: You have seen Horus at the neferu(?), and Thoth and Maat on either side of him.
sentences.n: mꜣꜣ·n·k is written here with one vulture. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone. ḥr nfrw: the face ḥr with its stroke is 'at, upon'; nfrw is the nfr sign with f, r, w, a kneeling man with an arm raised to his face (A2, approximate) and a flat bar with a small hanging tuft (Aa13, approximate) over plural strokes. Budge prints '(?)' over that bar in the sign line, unsure of the sign himself, and renders 'the place of look out'; the word is left untranslated here as 'the neferu(?)', and its sense is unknown. Thoth's name has no ibis (G26): it is spelled out with the hand d (standing for ḏ, as in later spellings), ḥ, w, t, y and the seated god. mꜣꜥt 'Maat' is the plinth with t and the goddess with the feather (C10, approximate). ḥr ꜥwy·f 'at his two arms' is the dual of ꜥ 'arm': U15 (standing for the arm ꜥ), a stroke and U15 again, y and w, with ·f and the two strokes of the dual after it, which are not read; Budge's numeral 48 stands inside it. Thoth and Maat stand on either side of the god in the bark.

morph.gloss: the neferu, a word not understood here, perhaps a place in the sun's bark (?) (noun; Budge: neferu, 'the place of look out', with a query)

sentences.l: gods · all · in · rejoicing · have-seen · they · Ra · coming · in · peace · to · make-live · hearts · of · spirits
sentences.i: All the gods are in rejoicing when they have seen Ra coming in peace to make the hearts of the spirits live.
sentences.n: nṯrw 'gods' is spelled out here without the flag: water n, t (for ṯ), r, w, the seated god and a stroke, the word spelled out sign by sign instead of with R8. nbw 'all' (the basket with w and a stroke) follows its noun; m ḥꜥꜥw 'in rejoicing' as above, without y. Budge prints maa en sen as three groups under one English, 'they see'; they are joined here into mꜣꜣ·n·sn, the sḏm·n·f of mꜣꜣ with ·sn 'they' (s, n, plural strokes), in a clause of circumstance, 'when they see'. iw 'coming' is the walking legs iw (printed before the chick) and w, the participle of iwi after rꜥ; m ḥtp 'in peace' is the offering table with t and p. r sꜥnḫ 'to make live' is r with the infinitive of sꜥnḫ, the causative of ꜥnḫ: s, the ankh, n and ḫ. ibw 'hearts' is one heart with two strokes; ꜣḫw 'the spirits' is the ibis (G25) with strokes and the kneeling figure with a flail (A52, approximate).

sentences.l: says(?) · Osiris · scribe · (of)-god's-offerings · of · lords · (of)-Thebes · Ani · true-of-voice · with · them
sentences.i: So says(?) the Osiris, scribe of the god's offerings of the lords of Thebes, Ani, true of voice, who is with them.
sentences.n: in is here the reed with the fish trap in (W25, approximate), another spelling of the word in line 39, and it is taken the same way, 'says N', closing the hymn; Budge gives it no English, and it is doubtful. It is less easy here than in line 39: the promises before it speak to Ani as 'you', so 'says N' must mean that Ani recites them for himself. Ani's title follows: sš ḥtp-nṯr 'scribe of the god's offerings'. Budge prints ḥetep and neter as two groups under one English ('of the divine offerings'); they are joined here into ḥtp-nṯr, the offering table with t and p and the flag with the seated god. n nbw wꜣst 'of the lords of Thebes' is n, the basket nb with plural strokes, and Waset, the sceptre wꜣs (R19, approximate) with t and the town sign. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw without the sickle. ḥnꜥ·sn 'with them' is ḥ, n, ꜥ with ·sn (here with the folded cloth s): Ani is among the gods and spirits just named. Spell 15 ends here; in Budge's edition Spell 133 begins on the next page.
